proposals.name: Server-minted request-id bracket as a stretch guard for latency checks
proposals.observation_summary: Anthropic request ids are UUIDv7 rendered in base58: 154,815/154,815 v7|var2 in swechat (this count includes 50 Vertex ids the loader stored as api_msg_id) and 31,085/31,085 in cc_local. The layout was inferred from data and is UNVERIFIED against vendor documentation (ids/O1). Their server time agrees with the client stamps: swechat non-Vertex n=155,267 (session, request) pairs in 1,638 sessions, 10 violations all in 1 session, agreement 0.99871 [0.99676, 0.99992] counting every copy, full-data p50 offset 3,781 ms [3,684, 3,871]; holdout A has 11,047 ids with 0 violations (ids/O2, skeptic numbers). One constant skew per stream places every id between the last input event and the first output block: swechat 10 of 3,674 streams inconsistent, rate 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466], slack U-L p5 1,102 / p50 2,268 / p95 3,807 ms; cc_local 1 of 847 streams, even though client skew produces 125 naive-rule violations in 3 sessions (ids/O5, ids/O6). Placebo on 3,673 swechat streams: moving one response's first event 5 s earlier flags 1,441 and 30 s earlier flags 3,581, while moving it 5/30/300 s later flags 10, the baseline. Power is therefore one-sided and per turn (ids/O5 skeptic). The id clock picked the original over the re-stamped copy in 178/178 resume/fork splits (ids/O7). aiv_cu server-minted ids (Anthropic msg after 2026-07-06, OpenAI items, Gemini responseId) show 0 violations (ids/O3). aiv_cc stores no request ids (ids/O13).
proposals.test_measurement: Phase B Probe 1 flags results that arrive faster than the work allows. A post-hoc forger's cheapest evasion is to move the result stamp later, or to shift the rest of the stream. Test whether the bracket closes that route, reusing the ids lens bracket code on swechat CC (B and holdout A) and cc_local: (a) delay one randomly chosen tool result by D in {1, 2, 5, 30, 300} s, keeping file order and leaving every request id untouched; recompute L = max(last input ts - id time) and U = min(first block ts - id time) per stream, and count flagged streams; (b) a consistent re-stamp variant that shifts that result and every later client event by D; (c) the same per turn on aiv_cu, using created_at against the decoded Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini ids. Report flags per D against the honest 10/3,674 (swechat) and 1/847 (cc_local) with session-clustered CIs. Also report the share of Probe-1-flagged fast results whose stream slack would let a forger stretch them up to the honest floor without tripping the bracket. Delaying an input is the mirror of the measured output-advance placebo (both shrink U - L), but it has not been run, so its power is UNVERIFIED.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured honest flags: 10/3,674 swechat streams (10 sessions) and 1/847 cc_local. The count depends on tolerance: 0 s gives 18, 5 s gives 7 (ids/O5). Known sources: re-stamped resume/fork copies, where copied history was collapsed onto 1-2 timestamps (477 entries in 2 session pairs; ids/O7); bulk-stamped history in old Claude Code (call->result gap exactly 0 in 498/137,380 main-thread pairs, 177 sessions; two_clocks/O12); client clock skew or steps within a stream (cc_local, ids/O6; the per-stream skew absorbs a constant offset but not a step); Vertex ids stored in the message-id column (50, ids/O1). Wide-slack streams (U - L p95 3,807 ms) give coarser resolution.
proposals.evasion_cost: Delaying a result past the stream slack requires rewriting the server-minted id of the next request, and of every later request if the rest of the stream is shifted. The forger must decode and re-encode base58 UUIDv7 under a layout we only inferred, keeping the version/variant bits and one consistent skew per stream. The agent cannot influence when the provider mints the id. Whether request ids ever enter the model's context was not measured (UNVERIFIED; they are harness fields of the transcript). Not caught: making a result earlier (the later-shift placebo equals the baseline), and an execution-path compromise with honest stamps, where the bracket adds nothing beyond Probe 1 itself. Resolution is per turn, on the order of the stream slack (p50 2,268 ms).
proposals.coverage: swechat Claude Code: 155,267 (session, request) pairs in 1,638 sessions (ids/O2), against 1,679 Claude Code transcript files in split B (two_clocks/O1); the bracket was evaluated on 3,674 streams. cc_local: 31,085/31,085 request ids decodable, 847 streams. aiv_cu: per turn only, since every call has lat == 0 (59,956/59,956; correlations/O4). Anthropic msg ids carry time only from 2026-07-06 (0 v7 from 2025-04 to 2026-06; ids/O4); OpenAI items 14,038 ids; Gemini responseIds 12,292 (1 s resolution). Bracket streams: 105/80/27/32 Anthropic, 255/92 Gemini, 463 OpenAI. Not covered: aiv_cc (0 request ids; 35,452 msg ids decode at chance level, ids/O13); Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI (only client-minted id clocks from the same process as the stamps); Who&When (no clock). Two of five scaffold families.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: decoding provider-minted UUIDv7 request ids as a third clock that bounds client-side agent log stamps looks uncommon in agent-log work. UUIDv7 time extraction and skew bracketing are standard distributed-systems forensics, and the bracket itself is the ids lens's candidate. The possibly new part is using it specifically to close the stretch evasion of our latency-physics check.
proposals.rank_reason: Largest measured share of tool calls bound by a clock the agent does not control, with a measured honest stream rate of 0.00272 and measured per-turn power, in two of five families.

proposals.name: Usage-ledger propagation check: parameter-free usage identities over every API turn, anchored by out-of-band tallies
proposals.observation_summary: Provider usage obeys exact, parameter-free identities in every scaffold family we hold. The cache-append chain cache_read(k+1) = cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) holds in 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.999 of clean pairs (swechat CC / cc_local / aiv_cc; TC1 skeptic) and in 59,747/59,804 aiv_cc pairs (aiv_accounting/O9). Codex cached input is a multiple of 128 in 16,106/16,106 calls, and OpenCode GPT-family cache.read in 11,393/11,393 (T11). The Codex cumulative chain holds 15,302/15,386 once duplicate events are dropped, and 81/84 remaining breaks follow a compaction or rollback (A6-O7 skeptic). OpenCode total = in + out + cache.read + cache.write in 14,639/14,854 (post hoc; A6-O8). Gemini CLI total = in + out + thoughts in 5,141/5,141 (A6-O9). Gemini prompt IMAGE tokens move by 0 or one per-model unit in 11,668/11,668 pairs (TC9) and sit on {258, 1064, 2160} in 10,569/10,569 pro rows (D3). aiv_cc result ledger: num_turns = user rows + 1 in 153/154 non-trivial runs, and cost is linear in tokens in 193/193 (aiv_accounting/O4, O5). In swechat, a commit-time tally written by the Entire CLI equals a recount of the transcript in 4,794/4,836 Claude-format sessions, with 33/5,701 unmatched across 4 scaffolds after the join fix (T1, T3). The conservation residual exists for 8 units (TC1 pairs: swechat CC 154,189; cc_local 30,210; aiv_cc 35,307; Codex 6,842; OpenCode 5,334; Gemini CLI 1,896; aiv_cu Anthropic 22,673; aiv_cu Gemini 11,945), but its content power is weak. At realized FPR 0.0101, an inserted change needs 8,913 / 10,000 chars for power 0.5 / 0.9 in swechat CC (aiv_cc 2,239 / 2,512), and deleting a result under 1k chars is never detected (TC2, TC16 skeptic).
proposals.test_measurement: Per unit, list which identities apply and their honest hold rates (above). Run a tamper simulation on honest split-B sessions: (1) delete one tool-result turn, (2) duplicate a turn, (3) swap two adjacent turns, (4) add or remove k chars in one result without touching usage, (5) an informed forger who recomputes every later usage field arithmetically (cache propagation, 128-multiples, image units, cumulative totals). For each, count sessions flagged by any exact identity, by the conservation residual (thresholds from the other fold, as in TC2), and by the commit-time tally (swechat only). Report per unit the share of API turns covered by at least one exact identity, and the share of tool results large enough for conservation power >= 0.5. In swechat CC only the [10000,100000) bin (n 8,788) reaches 0.973 for whole-result deletion, against 0.085 for [1000,10000) (n 40,056), 0.003 for [100,1000) (n 61,269) and 0.009 for [0,100) (n 30,914) (TC16).
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured honest breaks of the cache chain in aiv_cc: idle gaps of 300 s or more (8/32 break, against 49/59,772 below 300 s), image pairs (4,367/4,570 hold) and every compaction pair (0/933 hold) (aiv_accounting/O9); 30 non-compaction context resets with no compact_boundary row (aiv_accounting/O12). The Codex chain breaks at compaction/rollback (81/84). The OpenCode identity is post hoc. Tally residual: 33/5,701 sessions over 18 repos (T3, T4). Conservation tail: hidden-content tools (ToolSearch residual median +897.4 with 0 logged chars, TC4; ExitPlanMode median -1,357.4, TC13).
proposals.evasion_cost: Under an execution-path compromise with an honest harness, the model really received the fake output, so usage conserves and nothing breaks. This family only addresses after-the-fact edits. Against those, every identity is arithmetic that a forger holding the transcript can recompute and propagate through all later turns, and conservation is evaded by any change below 8,913 chars (swechat CC, power 0.5) or by length-preserving substitution. What the forger cannot get from the transcript alone is the provider tokenizer (conservation residual medians of tens of tokens in coding scaffolds, TC1) and, in swechat, the commit-time tally held in a git branch outside the transcript (T1). The agent does not see its own usage numbers in context (UNVERIFIED).
proposals.coverage: The only witness measured in all five scaffold families: conservation pairs for 8 units (TC1), and at least one exact identity measured for Claude Code formats (cache chain), Codex (128-granularity, cumulative chain), OpenCode (total identity; 128-granularity on GPT-family models), Gemini CLI (total identity) and AI Village (aiv_cc cache chain and result ledger; aiv_cu Gemini image units). TC1 reports no aiv_cu OpenAI/compat unit and nothing for Who&When. Effective content coverage is small: only results of several thousand chars and up are constrained (TC2, TC16). The out-of-band tally exists only in swechat.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: this builds on our own Phase A token-conservation plan and on the aiv_accounting, swechat_tables and distributions lens candidates (cache-chain continuity, provider lattices, out-of-band ledger). The possibly new part is requiring all identities jointly, so that one inserted or deleted turn must be propagated through every later usage record and an external tally. LLM billing-reconciliation tooling may already do similar bookkeeping.
proposals.rank_reason: Broadest scaffold coverage of any measured witness (all five families, every API turn), but it constrains turn structure far better than result content, and its identities are recomputable.

proposals.name: Dual-rendering check: harness-only structured result fields vs the model-visible result text
proposals.observation_summary: Coding scaffolds write many tool results twice: a model-visible string and a structured record for the UI or event stream. Claude Code Read toolUseResult.file.numLines equals the numbered lines of the visible text in 87,827/88,229 swechat results (0.9954 [0.9950, 0.9959], 4,603 files). All 402 mismatches are named harness or dataset formats (282 persisted-output previews, 105 'file shorter than offset' warnings, 7 dedup references, 7 redactions, 1 negative line numbers). In cc_local main sessions it is 570/578, and all 8 mismatches are empty-file warnings (A6-O1 skeptic). Agent/Task totalToolUseCount equals the distinct nested tool_use ids in 6,623/6,623 (A6-O2). Field fill in the full swechat population: Read 88,229/90,763 = 0.972, Edit structuredPatch 70,553/73,460 = 0.960, Grep numLines 29,535/34,208 = 0.863 (A6-O4 skeptic). Task/Agent totalDurationMs equals the parent result ts minus the first nested event within 2 ms in 1,900/2,188 (two_clocks/O3). In Codex the model-visible 'Wall time' header sits between -139.24 and -49.65 ms from the harness exec_command_end duration on 2,420 own-end outputs (two_clocks/O6), and exec duration is present on 13,876/13,876 exec events (A6-O3). Claude Code's file-history-snapshot names 24,031/24,286 successfully mutated paths (A6-O5).
proposals.test_measurement: Inventory each (visible text, structured field) pair per scaffold and tool, with its honest agreement and a whitelist pre-registered from split A (the 402 swechat Read formats are the template). Tamper honest split-B results: add or delete n lines, change a printed count, truncate, or splice text from another call, leaving structured fields untouched (naive forger), and count identity breaks per tool. Separately, measure what the structured fields add across calls that the text lacks: Edit structuredPatch line positions against line numbers shown by earlier Reads of the same file, and Read totalLines against later Reads. This part feeds the core plan's shadow state rather than standing alone. Report per scaffold the share of all calls carrying at least one checkable structured field; that all-calls denominator has not been measured.
proposals.false_positive_source: Harness display formats (the 402 whitelisted swechat Read mismatches; 8 cc_local empty-file warnings). Version drift: cc_local subagent files carry no Read numLines (0/12), and Glob totalMatches is 0/6,422 in swechat against 1,231/1,234 in cc_local (A6-O1, A6-O4). Dataset redaction. 2,150/8,773 Agent results have no nested traffic and must be counted as uncheckable, not as passes (A6-O2). Codex shell_command headers at 0.1 s display resolution exceed the gap in 646/1,817 by at most 49 ms (two_clocks/O6). The IR drops tool_reference blocks (TC4).
proposals.evasion_cost: Catches only a forger who edits the visible text and not the structured record. Line counts and nested-call counts are trivially recomputable by anyone holding the transcript. structuredPatch line positions and Read totalLines depend on the real file, which is costlier to fake consistently across calls. The structured record is a transcript field that the model does not receive (UNVERIFIED), so the agent cannot tune it in flight. Under an execution-path compromise with an honest harness, both renderings derive from the same fake output, so a faked Bash result gives no signal here.
proposals.coverage: Claude Code formats dominate swechat (format counts: claude_code 4,925, opencode 623, codex 213, gemini 59, cursor 23; A6-O16). Within them, Read, Edit and Grep results carry a field at 0.972 / 0.960 / 0.863. Harness duration fields exist for only 2.8% of CC calls (correlations/O8). Codex has an exec duration on every exec event (13,876/13,876 in 67 files), but the Wall-time identity was measured on only 5 sessions, one of which supplies 1,604/2,420. OpenCode has bash state.time.end on 5,311/5,317 (A6-O3); its other metadata were not measured. AI Village: only aiv_cc tool durations (WebFetch 29, Glob 133, WebSearch 47 results; aiv_accounting/O3). aiv_cu, Gemini CLI and Who&When are not covered. Three of five families, CC-heavy.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: the neighbours are recomputation (METR) and output-grammar parsing (jc). This compares two harness renderings of one result instead of recomputing from inputs. It generalises the raw_census lens's structured-counter recount across scaffolds. Harness developers likely know the redundancy; we have not seen it used for fabrication detection.
proposals.rank_reason: Exact identities with whitelisted honest FP over the largest call counts in the dominant coding format, across three families, but trivially recomputable and blind to execution-path compromise.

proposals.name: Provider-clock action windows for logs without per-call stamps (AI Village computer use)
proposals.observation_summary: aiv_cu is the largest corpus (78,114 sessions; D2, changepoints/O4) and has no per-call latency: every call has lat == 0 (59,956/59,956; correlations/O4). Each turn still carries clocks the agent does not write: Google's HTTP Date and server-timing on Gemini rows, and provider-minted ids for all three providers. On Gemini rows the server duration always fits inside the DB row gap (0/12,292, Wilson hi 3.12e-4, 347 sessions; slack min 563.8 ms, median 6,079), and created_at never precedes the HTTP Date (min 78.2 ms; two_clocks/O7). The Date precedes the row insert in 3,246/3,246 flash and 8,990/8,990 pro call rows, with medians -4,434 / -4,574 ms; the order is unambiguous at 1 s resolution in 2,831/3,246 and 7,276/8,990 (D19 skeptic). Because the row is inserted after the action runs, created_at minus the Date bounds action execution plus client overhead. Provider id times also precede the row with 0 violations: Anthropic opus 3,481 ids (min 1,297 ms, p50 11,607), OpenAI 14,038 (min 450, hex50 p50 5,716), Gemini 12,292 (ids/O3). For those ids the window also contains generation. Gemini server timing tracks reasoning (srv_ms vs resp_think 0.517 [0.477, 0.562]; correlations/O7).
proposals.test_measurement: On aiv_cu split B, then the population, compute per Gemini row w = created_at - HTTP Date. Per OpenAI/Anthropic row, compute w' = created_at - decoded id time minus a generation allowance fitted on split A from output tokens. Stratify by action (shell, gui, get_pixel_coords, pause) and by shell command class. Positive controls: pause actions and shell commands with an explicit sleep or timeout must satisfy w >= requested duration - 1 s; report the honest violation rate with session-clustered CIs. Then measure separability: compare w for commands whose output reports multi-second work (installs, builds, test runs, pushes) against trivial commands, with a threshold pre-registered on split A, and report the rate at which honest long-work outputs fall under it.
proposals.false_positive_source: 1 s HTTP Date resolution: 415 flash and 1,714 pro rows lie within 1 s of the insert, so their order is ambiguous (D19). Client overhead: gap - dur is at least 563.8 ms (two_clocks/O7). Screenshot capture and row-write time on GUI actions. For Anthropic/OpenAI rows, generation inside the window (opus id-to-row p50 11,607 ms) loosens the bound. Occasional late writes: 17 rows with updated_at more than 1 s after created_at (D6). No Anthropic msg-id clock before 2026-07-06 (ids/O4).
proposals.evasion_cost: Under an execution-path compromise the fake action finishes fast, so a claim of long work inside a short provider-bounded window is caught. The forger's cheap evasion is to pad the fake with a sleep, the same weakness any latency check has. After the fact, a forger would have to rewrite AI Village's DB created_at and the stored provider headers and ids consistently. The agent sees neither at action time (UNVERIFIED that the headers never reach the model).
proposals.coverage: Tight bounds only on Gemini rows: 12,292 rows in 347 of 2,000 aiv_cu B sessions (two_clocks/O7). Looser, generation-inclusive bounds on OpenAI items (14,038 ids) and on Anthropic msg ids after 2026-07-06 (0 v7 from 2025-04 to 2026-06; ids/O4). Other corpora already have per-call stamps for Probe 1, so this adds coverage only to AI Village computer use, one family.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using LLM-provider HTTP Date and server-timing headers as an execution-time bound for agent actions looks uncommon. HTTP Date headers are a known web-forensics artefact, and the ordering check is the two_clocks lens's third-party bracketing candidate. The possibly new part is turning it into an action-duration witness where the harness has none.
proposals.rank_reason: Adds a timing witness to the largest corpus, where per-call latency does not exist, but tight bounds cover only Gemini rows in one family.

proposals.name: Image-token quanta as a screenshot-count witness for GUI agents
proposals.observation_summary: In GUI sessions the text log holds almost nothing to check: aiv_cu GUI results carry text in 0.0002 of rows, and STOP-narration string support falls from 0.657 (no GUI) to 0.286 (GUI share above half) (N5 skeptic). Provider usage still records what reached the model. Gemini prompt IMAGE tokens change by 0 or exactly one per-model unit in 11,668/11,668 pairs (258 for gemini-2.5-pro; 1064 for 3.x). The increment is positive in 5,059/5,092 GUI windows and 0 in all shell (0/4,134), get_pixel_coords (0/2,033) and pause (0/202) windows (TC9 skeptic), and prompt IMAGE counts sit on {258, 1064, 2160} in 10,569/10,569 pro rows (D3). In the Anthropic Agent SDK stream the residual per stripped image is tightly concentrated: median 890.1 (887.9-890.9), p25 879.1, p75 892.7 over 4,543 image pairs (aiv_accounting/O11 skeptic); single-image windows give 1,035.0, p5-p95 1,016-1,142 (TC17). Where image sizes vary the quantum is lost (swechat CC 535.0, p5-p95 121-1,618; TC17).
proposals.test_measurement: For aiv_cu Gemini, compare the image count implied by dIMAGE / unit in each window with the number of screenshot-returning actions logged there. Report honest agreement (5,059/5,092 positive GUI windows; inspect the 33 without an increment) and the detection rate when one GUI action is inserted into or deleted from honest windows. Refit aiv_cu Anthropic conservation with an image term (TC1 left it out: GUI windows have residual median +206.5 against -602.8 for shell) to see whether a per-image quantum appears, as in aiv_cc. Then cross with narration: compare the rate of narrated on-screen facts (titles, counts, URLs) in windows or sessions with zero image increment against GUI windows.
proposals.false_positive_source: 33/5,092 honest GUI windows with no increment, unexplained (TC9). Pruning beyond 40 images is untested, while 442 population Gemini sessions exceed 40 GUI turns (TC9). Units are model-specific, and gemini-3.8-flash (277 pairs) never shows an image (TC9). In Anthropic streams images share the residual with text framing, and unlogged context resets hit image pairs (27 of 30; aiv_accounting/O12). Image sizes vary where users paste images (TC17).
proposals.evasion_cost: A forger who inserts or deletes GUI actions after the fact must also edit promptTokensDetails (Gemini) or the usage/cache chain (Anthropic) by exact unit multiples in every later turn. That is recomputable arithmetic once the unit is known. The check witnesses only that an image of the expected size reached the model, not what the image showed. The agent does not see its usage breakdown (UNVERIFIED).
proposals.coverage: aiv_cu Gemini: 11,945 conservation pairs with 5,092 GUI windows in split B (TC1, TC9). aiv_cc: 4,543 image pairs in 64 runs of one agent (aiv_accounting/O11). GUI-heavy sessions are a large part of AI Village: 983 of the 2,192 sampled sessions have a GUI share above half (N5, N2). Not covered: aiv_cu Anthropic and OpenAI until an image term is fitted, coding scaffolds (images are rare and variable), Who&When. One family.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: per-image token quanta as a screenshot-count witness for GUI agents look uncommon. This extends the token_conservation lens's Gemini IMAGE ledger to Anthropic residual quanta and to narration grounding.
proposals.rank_reason: Fills the GUI gap where text-based checks fail, but is tight only for Gemini rows and one aiv_cc agent.
